target_semantics_and_differences: Turbulent-looking image displacement; native noise/evolution replaces donor fractal algorithm.
ffmpeg_route_design: Generate one or two synchronized seeded Perlin guide fields with bounded octaves. For turbulent X/Y modes use independent fields; directional modes zero one component; bulge/twist modes use fixed-neighbor derivatives of one field, rotating the derivative vector for twist. Scale by signed pixel amount and the explicit edge-pin envelope, then actually sample source RGBA at the resulting coordinates. Use native displace only for its qualified format/map domain, explicitly encoding the neutral, signed scale and edge mode (the documented 8-bit neutral example is 128). For fractional, wider-range or floating-point requests outside that domain, pack source and an RGB guide strip into a checked same-format FFmpeg vstack canvas, use geq channel lookups to read guide values and bilinearly sample only the original source rectangle, then crop back to the original dimensions. Apply the same coordinates to source alpha. Clamp/wrap/mirror/blank decisions occur against source bounds, never the guide strip.

Declare actual native-map and packed-canvas dimension/format limits; no silent clipping of requested displacement. CI: Concrete schema/build admission; actual output correctness, alpha/color/time semantics and bounded resources; native GUI/browser GUI/CLI/stdio MCP/HTTP MCP parity. Use a coordinate-coded grid and controlled constant/vector guides to prove actual pixel relocation, sign and zero-amount identity. Verify pinning makes the selected edges stationary, gradient and twist rotate the displacement relationship, and blank/wrap/mirror/smear behavior never samples the guide strip. Qualify fractional/large displacement, transparent edges and float/HDR preservation; assert padded-dimension rejection and bounded allocation.

target_semantics_and_differences: Seeded cellular/Voronoi-style texture with nearest/second-nearest/site-derived modes, scale, offset, tiling and evolution. Canonical sites stay within their lattice cells and use a fixed 5x5 neighborhood, which bounds candidate work and covers the nearest two for this site-placement rule. ffmpeg_route_design: Generate a true bounded nearest-site cellular field in FFmpeg geq. For each output coordinate, enumerate a fixed 5x5 neighborhood of lattice cells, derive one deterministic seeded site per cell with jitter/evolution constrained to that cell, and maintain the smallest and second-smallest Euclidean distances F1/F2 plus the nearest site ID using finite expression terms. Compile the selected distance, F2-F1 boundary, site-color or named combined pattern from those values, then apply contrast/invert/overflow and output scaling. For tiled variants wrap the site identity on the tile lattice while retaining the correct neighboring site positions. Rust constructs constants and the finite expression; FFmpeg evaluates the pixels. Perlin and cellauto do not implement this route.

target_semantics_and_differences: Add monochrome or independent colored sample noise with explicit clip, preserve-headroom and wrap-unit variants in the canonical descriptor. EffectCraft clip=false corresponds to normalized modulo wrapping; FilmCraft clip=false preserves headroom. Keep those variants distinct. Native stochastic sequence replaces donor hash identity.
ffmpeg_route_design: Generate seeded native noise on a neutral grayscale carrier at the declared grain resolution. Subtract the carrier center to obtain a signed residual; replicate one residual into RGB for monochrome or use independently seeded residual planes for color. Scale the residual with the declared grain reconstruction and add it to straight source RGB in the declared working transfer. Preserve original alpha and re-premultiply.
